subject: Eval kickoff: PulsePath model-fit plan, data format & scoring
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Nair <aisha@pulsepathhealth.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@pulsepathhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Eval kickoff: PulsePath model-fit plan, data format & scoring

Hi Aisha + Liam,

Thanks again for the time today — great to hear more about the triage workflows you want to accelerate and the error modes your clinicians care about most. Below is a short recap and the proposed next steps so we can get a Redwood-hosted eval running next week.

Recap (quick):
- Goal: identify a model+prompt config that matches PulsePath's triage accuracy target (>= 88% macro F1 on critical false-negative class) while keeping 95th percentile latency < 150ms for live inference.
- Data: you have ~12k de-identified triage cases (text + structured fields) and a prioritized subset (~1.5k) for an initial scoring pass.
- Risk items: label consistency across raters, PHI handling, and edge-case free-text notes.

Proposed Redwood eval plan (high level):
1) You drop a prepared CSV (template attached) to the shared Drive folder. Columns: case_id, patient_age_bucket, notes, triage_label, rater_id, sealed_comments. We included optional columns for symptoms tags and facility_id.
2) Redwood runs 3 candidate model families across the set: a smaller fast variant (quantized 7B), a mid-size accuracy-first (13B fine-tuned / instruction-tuned), and a fallback Llama-derivative tuned for recall. We'll provide generation parameters and prompt templates.
3) Scoring: primary metric = macro F1 on triage_label; secondary = recall on 'urgent' class, and latency percentiles. We also run a per-prompt sensitivity check to detect regression vs. your seed prompts.
4) Output: per-case predictions, confidence scores, per-prompt calibration plots, and a regression alert if any model drops >3 points on your seed prompts vs baseline.

Attachments shared: pulsepath_dataset_template.csv (CSV), pulsepath_scoring_rubric_v1.md (rubric & thresholds), redwood_eval_instructions.pdf (ops checklist). Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PulsePathEvalSpecs

Ask: can you and Liam confirm the 1.5k subset will be available in the template format by Thu 8/6 EOD? Also flag if any records still contain PHI — we can accept an encrypted HMAC mapping but prefer fully de-id'd CSV for the eval.

Next internal steps from our side: I’ll loop in Ben for model recommendations and Marissa for scoring/ops once you confirm dataset availability.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

—
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Eval kickoff: PulsePath model-fit plan, data format & scoring

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear recap and the templates. A couple quick clarifications before we prep the subset: 

1) Labels: our triage_label is currently a 4-class enum (low, moderate, high, urgent). For the scoring rubric, should we map to a 3-class grouping (low/moderate / high / urgent) or keep the 4-class? We care most about recall on the urgent class.
2) PII: the dataset is de-identified but we still have free-text notes that occasionally contain facility identifiers. We can redact facility names; would a facility_id column (integer) suffice to preserve that signal?
3) Rater consistency: some cases have two annotations (rater1, rater2). The attached CSV template has a single rater_id column — do you want both in separate rows or aggregated?

We expect to have the 1.5k subset ready by Thu 8/6 EOD if the format matches the template. If you prefer, I can upload a redacted sample (n=50) today for you to sanity-check.

Thanks,
Aisha
Director of Clinical Ops, PulsePath Health
aisha@pulsepathhealth.com

Camila — good thread. Quick answers and an attachable micro-plan below.

Rater handling: please ask Aisha to provide both rater columns if available (rater1_id, rater2_id). We will:
- Ingest both; compute Cohen's kappa and report agreement.
- For primary scoring, produce two views: 1) adjudicated_label (majority/clinician-adjudicated if both differ) and 2) per-rater predictions so they can inspect disagreement cases.

Facility identifiers: facility_id (integer) is fine — keeps signal without PHI. Recommend they redact facility names and include facility_id.

Models & infra recs:
- Candidate family A: redwood-llm-7b-q4f (quantized 7B) — target for low-latency baseline. Expect median ~60–80ms on our hosted vCPU+GPU config; p95 may spike if multitenant.
- Candidate family B: redwood-13b-instr (13B instruction-tuned) — best accuracy pick; run as a warm instance.
- Fallback: redwood-recall-6b (tweaked for recall).

For a dependable p95 <150ms during eval (and for consistent comparison across runs), recommend using a short Dedicated trial (2 cards) for the run window — this reduces noisy p95 variance. We can run a quick latency baseline for you in Dedicated then rerun on Hosted for cost comparison.

Scoring checklist (to add to rubric):
- Primary: macro F1 (adjudicated_label).
- Secondary: recall_u (recall on 'urgent'), precision on 'urgent', calibration Brier score aggregated by confidence deciles.
- Stability: rerun on seed prompt set (n=200) and flag if any model drops >3 macro-F1 points vs baseline.
- Agreement: Cohen's kappa between raters per label.
- Edge detection: auto-flag free-text notes with OOV tokens or >3 negations for manual review.

Operational notes:
- Request a 50-record redacted sample in the template so we can confirm ingest scripts by EOD today.
- We will provide a short runbook: 1) data ingest & scrub, 2) model runs (3 variants), 3) scoring & artifacts, 4) regression check & comparison report.

I'll drop a link to the benchmark job and a quick latency baseline run once the sample is uploaded.

—
